requirements.title: Owner-only access to the webhook routes
requirements.rationale: A subscription sends the owner-only events of a workspace to a URL, so only the owner may configure one, and a task fork has none of its own.

criteria.condition: the owner of a repository workspace or the admin token calls one of the nine routes under /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/webhooks with a credential that is not a workspace-bound token and that, when it is a PAT, carries workspaces:write for the writing routes (create, update, delete, rotate-secret, ping, redeliver) or workspaces:read or workspaces:write for the reading routes (list, get, deliveries)
criteria.action: run the route's handler
criteria.contract: the route's success status: 201 for create, 204 for delete, 200 for the other seven

criteria.condition: one of the nine routes is called by an org member of the workspace, by a user with no access to it, by a workspace-bound token, or by a PAT without the scope the route needs
criteria.action: refuse the request before its handler runs and change nothing

requirements.title: Creating a subscription with a signing secret shown once
requirements.rationale: The receiver needs a secret to tell the hub's deliveries from anyone else's, and the hub must not be able to leak it afterwards.

criteria.condition: an owner or the admin token sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/webhooks with a valid url and optionally types, include_forks and description
criteria.action: store the subscription with a newly generated signing secret, write parley.webhook.create in the same transaction, set the subscription's position to the seq of that event, and answer with the subscription plus secret
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with body {id: UUID, workspace: the slug, url, types (default ['*']), include_forks (default true), description (default ''), state: 'active', created_by: the caller's user id or null for the admin token, created_at, updated_at, last_delivery_at: null, last_status: null, failing_since: null, secret: 'whsec_' followed by 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters}; one event parley.webhook.create with workspace the slug, the caller as actor, resource_type 'event_webhook', resource_id the id and metadata {webhook_id, host, types, include_forks}

requirements.title: Destination safety
requirements.rationale: Without it a subscription would let any workspace owner make the hub send requests into the hub's own network.

criteria.condition: a create, or an update that gives url, names a host that is, or that resolves to, a loopback, link-local, private, unique-local, unspecified, multicast or cloud-metadata address, over IPv4 or IPv6, while [webhooks].allow_private is false
criteria.action: refuse the request and leave the stored url as it was
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type webhook_destination_refused; no subscription is created, an existing subscription keeps its url, and no event is written

requirements.title: The signed delivery request and the outcome of an attempt
requirements.rationale: A receiver must be able to verify where a delivery came from and drop duplicates, and the hub must judge every attempt by one rule.

criteria.condition: the hub makes a delivery attempt for an event
criteria.action: send one HTTP POST to the subscription's url whose body is the event record as one JSON object, byte for byte as the event log returns it, with the headers Content-Type application/json, Parley-Event (the type), Parley-Delivery (the delivery id), Parley-Seq (the seq), Parley-Timestamp (Unix seconds at which this attempt is sent), Parley-Signature and User-Agent parley-webhook/<hub version>, and with no Authorization header, no cookie and no other header that identifies a user
criteria.contract: the receiver gets method POST on the url's path and query; the body equals the JSON object GET /events/log returns for that seq; the six Parley and User-Agent headers have the values named; Authorization and Cookie are absent
